text.p: The Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd (MRCB) and its associates are expected to announce a major restructuring plan on Monday, the daily Star reported on Saturday.
It said quoting a senior MRCB official that MRCB and associates New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd and Sistem Televisyen Malaysia Bhd (TV3) would announce a "complex restructuring exercise".
"The objectives which MRCB wants to achieve are simple but the restructuring is complex," the unnamed official was quoted as saying.
The shares of all three companies were suspended on Friday pending announcements. Their officials were not immediately available for comment.
MRCB is a diversified group with interests in power generation, media, property development and financial services.
MRCB owns a 48 percent stake in publishing group NSTP and 43.2 percent interest in TV3, which operates a private television station.
The Star did not give any details of the restructuring, but quoted MRCB executive chairman Khalid Ahmad as having said that the group should think some innovative measures rather than sell assets.

Last year, MRCB sold loss-making MRCB Telecommunications Sdn Bhd to Telekom Malaysia Bhd for 635 million ringgit and is finalising the acquisition of a 27 percent stake in stock broker Rashid Hussain Bhd.
Its associate NSTP has recently sold its 20.13 percent stake in Commerce Asset Holdings Bhd to FCW Holdings Bhd for 968.8 million ringgit.
